message: MCA Capital cover for BTG Pactual, Constellation Challenge 2021.
layout_trick: Dark navy full-bleed photo with a translucent dark band behind the title block and team names letter-spaced at the bottom; co-branding logos bottom-right.

message: BUY, target BRL 154.2 vs current 101.5 = 52% upside, supported by three theses.
layout_trick: Thin-bordered box with BUY highlighted in green and price-to-target connected by a line carrying the upside %, then a bottom strip with three numbered thesis tiles separated by x marks.

message: LatAm's largest investment bank is heading into digital retail; revenue split 48% capital-intensive vs 33% client-fee, plus 19% non-core.
layout_trick: Core-business box with big % next to each line, funnelling via a cyan trapezoid into a circular logo and then three launched digital units (with launch years) on the right.

message: Thesis 1 opens: BTG is the best surfer to ride the financial deepening wave.
layout_trick: Section divider with a vertical icon rail (one icon per thesis) where the active thesis is highlighted by a translucent box over the photo and the others are dimmed.

message: Brazil's capital markets are underdeveloped (3% of GDP vs 14% US) and falling rates drive credit costs down and issuance up.
layout_trick: Two-panel slide with a blue sentence-lead above each chart, Brazil bar flagged by a callout label, paired with a stacked-column issuance chart overlaid with a cost-of-credit line.

message: Wholesale is 94% of BTG's revenue vs 6-32% at retail banks, with 47% lead-coordinator, 84% seniority and 79% market share in ECM.
layout_trick: Single bar chart with BTG in dark navy against light-blue peers, beside three stacked teal tiles each pairing an icon, a giant % and a label; earlier build step greys out the right half.

message: BTG leads ECM mandates despite a smaller credit portfolio, and its credit book grew 280% in 2016-20 vs 35-78% for peers.
layout_trick: Scatter of mandates vs lending volume with a regression line and a BTG callout box plus peer logos as markers; paired with stacked-area chart carrying CAGR chips in brand colours.

message: Corporate lending: cheaper funding plus lower credit risk, and the SME receivables strategy gives low provisions + high spreads = margin gains.
layout_trick: Two proportional circles (R$53.6bn to R$107.2bn) plus a mini flow diagram and an equation strip with coloured tiles (Low Provisions + High Spreads = Margin Gains).

message: Falling Selic is driving greater volume and sophistication in Brazilian capital markets, with fund count and search interest rising.
layout_trick: Three charts on one slide (Selic line, fund-count stacked area, Google Trends) tied together by a dark quote strip citing an industry executive.

message: HNWIs are pushing BTG's AUM: 2020 HNWI assets grew 43% YoY.
layout_trick: Stacked AUM columns by client type with a curved light-blue arrow rising from the 2018 bar to a bold takeaway text, ending in a question box that hands off to the next slide.

message: BTG Private Banking is ranked #1 in Brazil's best PB services 2020, with more than 15 wealth-management awards.
layout_trick: 100%-stacked horizontal bars by client segment beside a podium-style 1st/2nd/3rd logo row, with the right side faded in the earlier build.

message: Wealth management is a R$3.6tn market in three segments; adding High Income Retail takes BTG's TAM from R$1.5tn to R$2.5tn, +74%.
layout_trick: Stacked column on the left aligned with horizontal labelled bands (barriers to entry, who serves them), and an arc-arrow between two big TAM figures with the % increase on it.

message: IFAs suit clients better than bank managers: advisors cover about 100 clients each vs 400 per bank manager, offering broad products, UX and close advice.
layout_trick: Mini value-chain on the left (brokers/banks > advisors > clients) with a numbered 1-2-3 list on the right and a boxed comparison of clients per manager.

message: IFAs are a central expansion pillar, hampered by regulation; XP's AuC and IFA count grew through 2021E with 17% market share.
layout_trick: Column chart of AuC with a registered-IFA line and a big XP logo plus 17% market-share callout; right panel builds into a regulation-change statement and a peer-case logo row.

message: BTG's team spoke to 39 IFA offices (22 BTG, 16 XP, 1 Safra); only 9% consider becoming a broker.
layout_trick: Real screenshot of the video call as evidence, with a large '39 IFA offices' headline and a thin progress bar showing 9% vs 91% to dramatise the finding.

message: BTG's weapon: sophisticated IFAs (HNWI, cross-sell, certified professionals) bring much greater value than standard IFAs that concentrate a large share of assets.
layout_trick: Two dotted-border logo clusters (sophisticated vs standard IFAs) each connected via a diamond bullet to a row of characteristics, ending with a 2-icon conclusion.

message: BTG matches XP on product (27% vs 13% standout) and trails slightly on technology (23% vs 13%), but 86% of advisors expect both to commoditise.
layout_trick: Side-by-side 100% stacked columns for Products and Technology (BTG > XP / equal / XP > BTG) with a dark verdict bar underneath and a bordered 'However...' box with the key stat.

message: Advisors describe an open channel to BTG executives (quotes from Cordier and Lifetime).
layout_trick: Two alternating quote bands, a round headshot on the right for the first and on the left for the second, with hex-shaped light-blue backgrounds and highlighted key phrases.

message: Access to the investment bank gives a distinct value proposition: a BlackBridge client case where the advisor called BTG immediately for corporate solutions.
layout_trick: Large video-call photo grid on the left, dark quote bar on the right with italic highlighted line, short case narrative with bolded facts below.

message: Encouraging cross-sell benefits all stakeholders: BTG Digital + Robust Bank Structure + Open Channel + Right Incentives make BTG more efficient at cross-sell vs XP.
layout_trick: Vertical Company-Advisor-Investment Bank chain with green checks, contrasted against XP's chain with red X boxes in the earlier build; final 'In short' 3-icon equation.

message: There is a clear winner, and there are two: brokers/challengers rise to 40% of the market by 2025E and BTG and XP lead the WuC share.
layout_trick: Stacked columns of investment market with a % share line, linked by a thin line to a donut (R$2.3tn centre) with the BTG, XP and others WuC shares labelled.

message: Open Banking is traditional banks' nightmare: current-account concentration of the top 5 banks falls from 67.1% to 59.2%, ending the data monopoly.
layout_trick: Stacked columns with a concentration line, a green mini-legend box numbering the causes, and a dark callout strip plus a 3-step slanted-tile flow for the change.

message: Banks (product-oriented) vs fintechs (customer-oriented): BTG combines both, with a profitable IB structure (R$3.8bn 2019 net income) and a fully digital retail entrance.
layout_trick: Two opposing hexagonal panels (Product-oriented vs Customer-oriented) meeting at a central circular BTG logo, with a mini net-income bar chart on the left and a pentagon on the right.

message: Card adoption is easy (2.2x active cards per account) but recurrence of use is the tricky part; BTG+ is expected to solve it.
layout_trick: Two-line time series (checking accounts vs active cards) with a big '2.2x' ratio callout on the plot and a dark box delivering the conviction statement plus 'Why?' hook.

message: Highly integrated platforms (BTG+, BTG Digital) create a feedback cycle with a two-touch redirect from current account to investments.
layout_trick: Three phone mockups on a horizontal arrow labelled 1st touch / 2nd touch / arrived, with start and end labels at the edges of the line.

message: Ecosystem stickiness: customers enter via low-switching-cost BTG+ and end up in a high-switching-cost layer (BTG Digital, SME Lending).
layout_trick: Vertical stack of three product tiles on the left joined by LOW and HIGH chevrons pointing to a numbered 3-step explanation panel.

message: An even larger feedback cycle: investment bank (core business) and digital bank (DRU) reinforce each other through origination, IB products, funding and IFA proposition.
layout_trick: Two big circular arrows (dark and light blue) around a central logo with DRU and Core Business labels and four satellite text blocks at the diagonals.

message: From a small proprietary desk in 1983 to a global industry leader: key milestones 1989 licence, 2005 core expansion, 2011 Pan, 2012 LatAm, 2016 DRU.
layout_trick: Vertical-staircase timeline with year labels and short captions branching from a top box, bridging to the three success-factor tags that appear in the next build.

message: BTG's partnership model drives business-scope expansion: never in a comfortable position, integrated units, lean structure unlock new business units.
layout_trick: Three horizontal tag bars converge into a large dark-blue arrow pointing right to a 'unlocks value from new business units' statement; the timeline sits to the left.

message: Partners enter at book value and may sell at the lowest of book or market value, keeping them sharp: ROE averaged 15% in four years and partner equity returns are higher for those who stayed.
layout_trick: ROE line chart with a dotted average line at 15% and labelled troughs/peaks, beside a column chart of partners' equity; header strip with the three-pillar labels at the top.

message: The partnership model promotes integration: revenue by business unit grows at 32% CAGR with cross-selling lifting all areas, 'the whole cake must grow and not just the slice'.
layout_trick: Cake metaphor illustration (small cake growing into big cake) on the left next to a stacked-area chart with CAGR labels per layer on the right edge.

message: G7 Holdings, André Esteves and 237 partners control the bank, with the Senior Partners holding 87% of voting power through ON shares.
layout_trick: Compact ownership org chart (holding > BTG Holding > BPAC11 units, free float 26.1%) beside ON vs PN bar charts, with a highlighted callout for the 87% voting power.

message: Senior partners choose the best successors: the 2008 and 2021 controller classes show a deep bench (Esteves, Sallouti, Arida and new partners).
layout_trick: Large portrait of the former founder with a quote overlay and a 'we talked to' dark caption bar; right column stacks two lists of partners beside round/diamond portraits per era.

message: Pérsio Arida says BTG is the only banking case in history that suffered a full-fledged run and survived without a bailout.
layout_trick: Cut-out portrait bleeding off the left edge with a speech-style quote on a grey card to the right and a 'we talked to' black bar at the bottom for provenance.

message: Talent magnet: the partnership attracts great minds; Vice Chairman interview says BTG is not a rigid, bureaucratic place.
layout_trick: Five portraits cropped into a diamond-shaped mosaic with name labels, paired with a dark quote box on the right.

message: Amos Genish (Head of Digital Retail) leads with a telecom background: 6th-largest retail bank, 1st for IFAs and investors, 4.5 million customers by 2023.
layout_trick: Full-height cut-out executive photo on the left, short bio and logo clusters, with three teal stat tiles on the right, closing with a dark 'They don't have the digital DNA' statement.

message: BTG's ESG alignment is scored via an original index: current efforts (E/S/G criteria) vs future commitment (graded 1-3).
layout_trick: Diamond 'Index Rationale' node in the middle linking two boxes (current efforts, future commitment) to their criteria lists, with a benchmark logo rail down the right edge.

message: BTG is well positioned on ESG: current efforts vs future commitment scatter puts it above most peers, with E, S and G each backed by a highlight.
layout_trick: Scatter plot of peers (current vs future) with BPAC11 highlighted by a line to three stacked teal tiles (Environmental, Social, Governance) with one-line justifications.

message: Cross-selling drives corporate lending (R$73.7bn to R$209.7bn, 4.1x leverage) and IB revenue growth in the core business.
layout_trick: Two same-style column panels with tiny coloured % chips on every bar, a yield box in the corner and one assumption in the subtitle highlighted in blue.

message: Sales and trading revenue is forecast at 10% CAGR, discounting growth by 4.5% due to the VaR reduction from the retail insertion.
layout_trick: Column chart with a curved arrow and 10% CAGR label, paired with a mini step-by-step panel showing guidance range 450-850 to 600 and a 4.5% discount.

message: BTG Digital will reach R$515bn AuC by 2025 with three investor portfolios and an average take-rate of 0.72%.
layout_trick: AuC columns with BTG's share-of-brokerage line next to three profile tiles (conservative, moderate, aggressive take-rate) and a dark bar with the average.

message: BTG+ will reach 4.8 million customers and R$900 million annual profit via a bottom-up customer build.
layout_trick: Row of circular bubbles (81k to 4.8m clients) above a TPV column chart, with a stack of grey tiles listing each key assumption with its big number (1.5%, 1.1%, 10%).

message: Revenue reaches R$26.0bn by 2025E (22.9% CAGR) with the Digital Retail Unit at 29.4% of revenue and core business falling to 58.6%.
layout_trick: Stacked revenue columns by line with a right-side mix table comparing 2020 to 2025E; each segment gets a coloured box with %s so the mix is readable without a legend.

message: Asset-light expansion makes the bank more cost-efficient: efficiency ratio falls to 39.3% and net income grows to R$10.2bn.
layout_trick: Bars with an efficiency-ratio line labelled in dark chips, a dark blue headline tag above, and a second panel for payout ratio held at 60% in perpetuity.

message: Attractive returns combined with a healthy balance sheet: ROAE rises from 17.6% to 25.9% while Basel ratio stays above 16%.
layout_trick: ROAE/ROAA line chart on the left and a Basel index stacked column (Tier I / Tier II) on the right; two linked panels each led by a blue-underlined sentence.

message: SOTP valuation gives a R$154.2 price target with 52% upside: BPAC11 is the sum of core IB (R$101.9) + digital units.
layout_trick: Cascade from Investment Bank to BTG Digital, BTG+ Business, BTG+, Pan, Too Seguros to Total Share Value R$154.2, then current R$101.5 and a curved arrow showing upside; assumptions (Ke 11.92%, g 7%) on a dark side panel.

message: BPAC11 trades like incumbent banks despite a more attractive growth story, so we believe the stock is underpriced.
layout_trick: P/BV vs ROE scatter with a shaded 'Challenger' zone and a regression line, BPAC11 highlighted, and a dark conclusion box at the bottom right.

message: Would you be a BTG shareholder? Yes: diversified businesses, driven by financial deepening, with an exceptional partnership model.
layout_trick: Dark closing slide with three stacked, right-pointing arrow banners in decreasing blue tones and a large italic 'Yes!' as the punchline.

message: IFA migration is not a nightmare: sophisticated IFAs migrate on average 82% of AuC in the first months vs 44% for common IFAs.
layout_trick: Three curved stream bands with icons (relationship, quantity, sophistication of services) lead into two big-number tiles (82% vs 44%), then a dark takeaway bar.

message: BTG has 60 IFA offices in the south-east concentrated in São Paulo vs XP's wider geographic spread (302 in SP).
layout_trick: Two identical choropleth maps of Brazil side by side (BTG vs XP) with gradient legends and state counts, making the footprint contrast obvious at a glance.

message: Tangerine case: despite a 100% digital proposal it needed physical contact, as 41% of Brazilians trust the bank manager to invest.
layout_trick: Building photo and CEO photo framing a large quote, with a flag + big 41% fact line in a grey bar at the bottom.

message: BTG Digital's metrics align with major international consolidated players, so the assumptions are sustainable.
layout_trick: Dense dark-header comps table with BTG's row highlighted in a grey band, followed by a one-line conclusion in blue.

message: BTG Digital sensitivity: each bank-unit share value responds to take rate and efficiency rate, take rate fixed at 0.72%.
layout_trick: Two red-yellow-green heatmap grids side by side (take rate x efficiency; efficiency x market share) with the base case at the top-left and a concise bullet explanation below.

message: BTG & Mosaico partnership creates value: cash-back service, more client retention and purchase recurrence expand BTG+ at near-zero CAC.
layout_trick: Central circular arrow with partner logos flanked by three left and three right feature labels with round connector dots, and a bottom three-step process timeline.

message: BoostLAB makes BTG the startups bank: each side (BTG, startup) gains customer base, cross-sell, equity opportunities and market reach.
layout_trick: Mirror layout with two dark tabs (BTG side left, Startup side right) and three symmetric labelled items per side joined by round markers.

message: Banco XP is a threat to traditional banks: total AuC R$ 205bn at BTG vs up to R$1.96tn at Bradesco, XP has a full-service licence plus Visa deal.
layout_trick: Chevron arrow ribbon summarising XP's evolution milestones next to a sorted peer column chart with BTG highlighted in blue and others in grey.

message: Our ESG Index scores BPAC11, ITUB4, BBDC3 and peers on E, S and G questions (1-3) and ranks them.
layout_trick: Dense scoring matrix with per-category subtotals and an average column; useful as an evidence appendix that supports the ESG slide.

message: ESG commitment is plotted as management vs stakeholders view; materiality focuses on data protection, ethics, and integrity.
layout_trick: Triangular materiality matrix with management-view on X and stakeholder-view on Y, coloured dots legend on the right and bolded highlights.

message: Trade-off between keeping the partnership model or going public: US banks IPO'd (Bear Stearns 1985 to Lehman 1994) and Goldman was the sole exception until 1999, then grew.
layout_trick: Vertical step-staircase of IPO dates and logos on the left against a revenue column chart with a CAGR bar on the right.

message: Goldman's partnership grew bloated (220 to 550 partners, profit per partner from US$1.8mn to 0.9mn): is BTG destined to the same?
layout_trick: Compact two-row 1999 vs 2020 comparison with a dotted bracket on the partner count, a WSJ headline clip as evidence, and a quote panel on the right.

message: BTG's executives are the maximum representation of its culture: Sallouti, Dias, Cardoso, Flora and Rapoport, with 20+ years at the bank.
layout_trick: Hero profile (photo, mini career timeline Intern to CEO, awards and board seats) above a row of four portrait-led executive cards.

message: BTG Pactual shareholder structure: G7 Holding 22.8%, partners and others, with free float 26.1% and BTG Holding Financeira 73.9%.
layout_trick: Clean ownership organogram with boxed holding entities, ON/PN share splits inside each node and percentages on connectors.

message: Investment bank industry dynamics: a bank earns fees from companies and investors across ECM/DCM/M&A, lending, S&T, AM and WM.
layout_trick: Vertical stack of the business lines in blue shades on the left, flanked by icons for companies and investors and a mini timeline of banking eras on the right.

message: BTG's average incentive fee in ECM deals is the highest (0.39%) of the peer set, indicating service quality.
layout_trick: Formula strip (Bank's economics x deal incentive fee = bank's incentive fee) above an ascending bar chart with BTG highlighted dark navy at the end.

message: Sales and Trading revenue (39% of revenue) is generated by fees and commissions and gains from trades, and growth will be driven by volume, client relationship and volatility.
layout_trick: Partial donut with the S&T slice pulled out and annotated with two numbered explanation boxes, and three dark icon tiles listing the growth drivers.

message: BTG takes more risk (VaR) than peers but with higher returns; risk profile is more diversified than competitors.
layout_trick: 100% stacked bars of RWA by risk type for five banks, beside a VaR line with industry-average shaded band behind it.

message: BTG is the highest in equity (19%) and hedge funds (32%) among banks in AM: AuM R$144bn.
layout_trick: Peer AuM table with BTG row highlighted in a teal band and column-shaded categories, next to a bar chart of AuM by fund class.

message: SME lending: operational advantages (collateral on cash flow) allow margin gains with low provisions and high spreads.
layout_trick: Two-line chart of SME vs large corporate credit with a labelled data-gap annotation, plus a recurring flow diagram and the Low Provisions + High Spreads = Margin gains equation.

message: BTG's unsecured funding doubled to R$107.2bn in 2020, pushed by the DRU, reducing credit risk and funding costs.
layout_trick: Horizontal funding stack by year with dotted bracketing of demand deposits and growth chips; right column shows BTG+ loan book column chart and two icon-led benefit boxes.

message: BTG's LatAm expansion: Colombia (since 2012) and Chile (since 2012) offer full investment-bank licence; ECM LatAm market and BTG share trends.
layout_trick: South America map with Colombia and Chile highlighted and attached labels carrying the acquisition and licence, next to two bar panels of ECM volume and market cap.

message: Banco Pan's synergy: BTG co-controls with Caixa, and covers low-income classes C-E (90% of population) that BTG does not serve.
layout_trick: Ownership box diagram on the left and an income-class pyramid (A to E) on the right with High income focus (BTG) vs Low income focus (Pan) labels.

message: Banco Pan's credit operation is growing: 80% of origination via INSS payroll loans, plus vehicles and credit cards.
layout_trick: Three donut charts with product icons feeding a bar-pyramid age distribution of the INSS niche.

message: Pan's competitive edge: it does not depend on fee-based revenue streams, compared with Santander, Bradesco, BB, Banrisul and digital peers.
layout_trick: Two peer tables with logos and revenue/ratio and product columns, grouping banks vs digital players, in light-grey zebra rows.

message: Too Seguros offers a good cross-sell optionality, with revenue and net profit trends since its 2018 rebranding.
layout_trick: Stacked bars (revenue and net profit) plus ROE line on the right with a left-hand ownership/relationship diagram using the logos.

message: Revenue breakdown by business line 2020-2025E, with each unit's share of total.
layout_trick: Hierarchical table with shaded sub-total rows (core, digital, others) and % of total beneath each line.

message: Corporate lending forecasts: SME yield of 6.4% vs large companies' 2.5%, with portfolio volume/book value to 4.11x by 2025E.
layout_trick: Forecast table split into sections (total, SME, large) with a side annotation and arrow explaining the yield-spread source.

message: Key balance sheet ratios 2020-2025E: ROE annualised 17.6% to 25.9%, Basel ratio 16.7% to 17.0%.
layout_trick: Cleanly bordered ratio table with dark header row and grouped line items (assets, capital, ratios).

message: AM and PB modelling rationale: AuM+AuA reach R$ 337.7bn with 19.8% CAGR, private banking volume grows at 15.2% CAGR.
layout_trick: Two stacked-column panels each with a large curved CAGR arrow over the bars and a bold ROA line at the base.

message: Equity value per business unit: Core is worth R$92.1bn (R$101.9/share), while Digital, BTG+ Business, BTG+, Pan and Too are the remainder.
layout_trick: Two bar panels (equity value vs per-share value) with the Core bar towering over the digital units so the weight of each unit reads immediately.

message: Implied multiples on the SOTP valuation and IRR sensitivity to exit P/E (16x-20x) and year give returns of 20.5% at 18x in 2023.
layout_trick: Clustered columns of implied multiples by unit next to an IRR grid (exit year x exit P/E) with the base case highlighted in dark and gradient blue cells.

message: Justified P/BV of 2.13x (ROE 17.5%, Ke 11.92%, g 7%) is compared with forecast P/BV falling from 3.6x to 1.8x by 2025.
layout_trick: Formula strip (Fair P/B = (ROE-g)/(Ke-g)) in a grey panel above a dashed forecast line against a shaded justified-P/BV band.

message: Sanity check: if BTG were on the P/BV-ROE regression line it would trade at 4.22x, nearly double the implied multiple.
layout_trick: Scatter plot with shaded 'Challenger' region, regression line equation box with a callout pointing to the result and a modest disclaimer note.

message: Valuation sensitivity to Ke vs g and payout in perpetuity: upside ranges 5%-131%; BUY stands for multiple scenarios.
layout_trick: Two red-to-green heatmaps showing % upside (Ke x g, Ke x perpetuity payout) with a BUY recommendation tag below the grid.

message: Leverage vs SME share of lending: upside holds between 43% and 61% across all combinations.
layout_trick: Single clean green-gradient grid with the base case in a bolder tile and large readable numbers, a good minimal sensitivity layout.

message: Economic uncertainty is the biggest threat: market, company and competition risks plotted by probability x impact.
layout_trick: Probability x impact grid with pill-shaped bubbles coded M1/M2 (market), C1-C3 (company), D1/D2 (competition) in three colours, with a coloured legend panel on the right explaining each code.
